item.title: Safe Diffusion Policies for Robot Learning
item.description:
Project Summary

Diffusion policies have shown strong performance on complex, multimodal robot control tasks, but they offer no inherent guarantees against unsafe behavior at inference time — a critical gap for long-horizon decision-making in safety-sensitive settings. This project investigates inference-time safety mechanisms for diffusion policies, aiming to shape or filter the denoising process itself so that generated action sequences respect safety constraints without retraining the underlying policy.

To study this, I built a PyTorch training and evaluation framework for Diffusion Transformer policies spanning both navigation and manipulation domains, enabling controlled experiments on the tradeoff between safety intervention and task performance. Early experiments on path-planning tasks show promising results, while receding-horizon control and manipulation settings surface open challenges around closed-loop consistency when safety interventions interact with the policy’s own multi-step denoising dynamics.

Principal Researcher (Mar 2026 — Present)

  • Investigating inference-time safety mechanisms for diffusion policies in long-horizon robot decision-making.
  • Built a PyTorch training and evaluation framework for Diffusion Transformer policies across navigation and manipulation domains.
  • Designed experiments on safety-performance tradeoffs and closed-loop consistency, demonstrating promising path-planning results and identifying challenges in receding-horizon control and manipulation.

Tech: PyTorch, Diffusion Transformers, robot learning, path planning, Gymnasium.

item.title: Continuous Offset-Based Coverage Paths for Planar Regions
item.description:
Undergraduate research project, 2022

Key ideas explored

  • A geometric distinction between local and global self-intersections in contour-parallel offset curves, and how they affect coverage continuity.
  • Use of medial-axis width structure to reason about when offsetting causes a region to split, and how modifying width can prevent topological disconnection.
  • A simple pre-processing technique that converts a family of offset loops into a single spiral-like continuous path.
  • Identification of sharp-turn regions induced by offsetting and localized smoothing without globally altering equidistance.

Limitations and scope

  • This work does not claim empirical superiority over existing infill or coverage strategies used in modern additive manufacturing.
  • The approach prioritizes geometric continuity over material optimality, and is most relevant to contexts where uniform coverage and motion smoothness dominate.
  • The algorithms are primarily geometric and exploratory; no large-scale benchmarking or hardware validation was performed.

In hindsight, this project shaped how I think about the relationship between geometric structure, modeling assumptions, and real-world relevance. Many of the limitations of this work informed my later focus on formally scoped, validated methods in safe learning and control.

Follow-up: Corner Smoothing for Additive Manufacturing Toolpaths (May 2021 — Aug 2021)

As a natural extension of the coverage-path work above, I later proposed a corner-smoothing method for additive manufacturing toolpaths, aiming to achieve uniform coating while constraining maximum curvature. I refined the original formulation into a convex optimization problem enforcing continuous curvature and even area coverage, implemented an iterative gradient-based solver in Python, and integrated it into the parallel-curve toolpath planner from the coverage-path project.

Research Assistant (May 2021 — Aug 2021)

  • Proposed a corner smoothing method for additive manufacturing toolpaths to achieve uniform coating while constraining maximum curvature.
  • Refined the original formulation into a convex optimization problem to enforce continuous curvature and even area coverage.
  • Implemented an iterative solver (gradient-based) in Python and integrated it into a parallel-curve toolpath planner.

Tech: Convex optimization, Python.
